answer: One concrete defense is staking with slashing. Each agent must lock a non-refundable deposit before it can transact, so minting a thousand fake identities costs real capital instead of being free. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a quartz layer, and cannot be faked overnight. Validators watch the delta between an agent's claimed activity and its on-ledger history; any mismatch gets its stake slashed. That hard cost floor stops attackers from spinning up cheap, disposable ivory personas that collect one payout and vanish.
